v.
DAVID GRAHAM, JUSTIN GRAHAM,
DONALD GRAHAM and DENNIS GLATT,
Defendants.

First Dakota National Bank ("First Dakota"), for its causes of action against Defendants
David Graham, as well as Drs. Justin Graham, Donald Graham and Dennis Glatt ("Defendants"),
states and alleges as follows:
GENERAL ALLEGATIONS
I.
First Dakota is a national bank and "regulated lender" under the laws of the State of
South Dakota and the United States of America, with its principal place of business located in
Yankton, Yankton County, South Dakota and branch locations throughout South Dakota.
Huron Hospitality II, LLC, ("HH LLC") is a South Dakota limited liability company
2.
that owned and operated the "Crossroads Hotel & Event Center" a/k/a "Huron Event Center" in
Huron, Beadle County, South Dakota.
First Dakota was a secured creditor of HH LLC. When HH LLC defaulted on its
3.
payments and committed multiple other non-monetary defaults, First Dakota placed HHLLC in a
receivership and foreclosed on the real estate secured by its note and mortgage. See First Dakota
National Bank v. Huron Hospitality II, LLC, Third Circuit, Case No. 12-593.
4.
At the time of loan to HH LLC, it was the sole record owner of the mortgaged
property. Each one the Defendants was a unit owner of HH LLC, who, in fhrtherance of the
debtor/creditor relationship between First Dakota and HH LLC, each signed separate Commercial
Guarantees as additional security for the loan. True and correct copies of each of the Guarantees
signed by each of the Defendants are attached hereto as Exhibits 1-4 and incorporated by reference.
5.
The G uarantees made each of the Defendants jointly and several lyliabl e for the debts
and obligations HH LLC owed to First Dakota under its note and applicable law. A true and correct
copy of the note guaranteed by the Defendants is attached hereto as Exhibit S and incorporated
herein.

EFTA01128803

 6.
Once the foreclosure process was completed and the redemption period expired,First
Dakota employed a commercial real estate agency (NAI of Sioux Falls, South Dakota) to list and
market the real estate while it continued to be managed by Kelly Inn, which was the court appointed
receiver.
Despite its best efforts,NAI was not successful in selling the property and its listing
7.
agreement with First Dakota has now expired. First Dakota remains the sole record owner of the
foreclosed real estate.
8.
After the NAI listing expired, First Dakota informed the Defendants through their
counsel in writing that it would seek to enforce its Guarantees unless one or more of the Defendants
made satisfactory arrangements with the bank to take an assignment ofthe real estate and guarantees
or pay the debts incurred by the bank while it continues to employ Kelly or another management
company to run the hotel. Because the Defendants failed to comply,FirstDakota brought this action
to enforce the Defendants' Guarantees.
